intent: Research sealed counterfactual lead MS-0121 as an Evidence-first bottleneck-stage decomposition for HBM during 2023-2026. Test the alternative to treating HBM shortage as synonymous with DRAM-wafer shortage by preserving wafer/input constraints, HBM die/TSV-stack production and yield, advanced packaging or GPU-package capacity, customer qualification, customer supply and platform availability as distinct stages. Reuse already-grounded HBM3E sampling/production/customer-supply/platform evidence and add only missing claim-scoped evidence that locates or bounds bottlenecks. Do not infer one universal binding constraint, convert product sampling into qualification, convert HBM production into packaged-GPU availability, or treat packaging-capacity tightness as proof of DRAM-wafer scarcity.
rationale_summary: Existing HBM3E trajectories already preserve supplier sampling, mass/volume production, later customer supply and H200 market availability as separate time-correct states. MS-0121 should therefore avoid another generic HBM-demand packet and instead recover bounded stage-specific evidence for where capacity can bind: HBM wafer/die supply, TSV/stacking or packaging throughput/yield, advanced GPU packaging, and customer qualification. The result should support a multi-stage bottleneck representation rather than a single synthetic HBM-scarcity scalar.
